Read in full in findings.json and docs/delivery/reviews/DG6/round-5/domain-reviewer.findings.json. (1) The round-5 reproduction re-run on the fixed repository (HEAD c9eca6539, Node 24.21.0): validate.mjs --historical --stage DG5, DG4, DG3, DG2 and DG1 each print 'PASS gate DGn (historical)' and exit 0 (round 5: FAIL 'DG6 illegal transition VERIFYING -> REVIEWING', exit 1); --pipeline prints 'PASS pipeline (active stage: DG6 REVIEWING)', exit 0; --register DG6 PASS. The first DG5 log's header shows HEAD 3c07fa84e because the orchestrator's c9eca6539 commit (state field FIXING -> REVIEWING) landed during that run; I re-ran it at c9eca6539: PASS, exit 0 (log 40b). (2) Mutants served in memory to the unchanged validator (node --import stages-serve-mutant.mjs; the repository is not changed; log 41): M1 removes only the DG6 entry {FIXING, 2026-11-11T06:42:33Z}, which reverts the fix: --historical DG5, DG1 and --pipeline each FAIL with exactly 'stages.json: DG6 illegal transition VERIFYING -> REVIEWING', exit 1; M2 puts back the state field of 3c07fa84e (FIXING while the last entry is REVIEWING): all three FAIL with 'DG6 state FIXING differs from last history entry REVIEWING', exit 1; the control M0 (HEAD content re-serialized) PASSES all three, exit 0. So the validator catches a revert, and the added entry alone is what makes it pass. (3) Consistency of the fix: the DG6 history now reads ... REVIEWING (round 3) -> VERIFYING 06:08:46Z -> FIXING 06:42:33Z (the commit time of the round-4 audit record 9610047bc; the note says it was recorded late, after F-DG6-911) -> REVIEWING 11:32:40Z (round-5 freeze) -> FIXING 14:42:55Z -> REVIEWING 14:42:56Z (round 6); all legal transitions, in time order; state REVIEWING equals the last entry; candidate, review_rounds 5 and 6 and gates/DG6.json (still BLOCKED, round 4) agree. The scan for other inconsistencies found two out-of-order timestamps in the approved gates DG0 and DG5 (not DG6, no gate decision depends on them): reported separately as F-DG6-952 (Low).

Its reproduction was --pipeline plus --historical --stage DG5..DG1, all exit 1 at 8754f809d. On the fixed repository (HEAD c9eca6539) all six exit 0 ('PASS pipeline (active stage: DG6 REVIEWING)', 'PASS gate DGn (historical)'), and --register DG6 passes (logs 40, 40b). The revert mutant M1 (the one added entry removed) brings back exactly the round-5 problem in --pipeline and --historical (exit 1), and M2 (the 3c07fa84e state field) is caught by the state-vs-last-entry rule (log 41). The audit's BLOCKED decision stays recorded in gates/DG6.json and the FIXING period of T-DG6-BE-RG3 is now in the history, which is what my finding asked for.

Verified as a non-author on candidate sha256:5e819f7a579dbf98eb78f7f8e326a7ad57d939ed6a0762e3bea912f6dc735ed6 (source 3c8b9a3ac; product tree equal to 60787d89f, git diff empty). Read in full in findings.json and docs/delivery/reviews/DG6/round-4/release-auditor.findings.json. (1) The round-4 reproduction, unchanged: the release auditor's probe zz-aud-r4-served-dg-labels.test.ts in a disposable clone, on a disposable PostgreSQL 16.15 migrated 0001-0130 (122 files), prints 'served strings naming DG0-DG7: 0' (round 4: 24) and passes; the shipped scan (d) seeded-texts.test.ts passes 4/4 in the same run (log 30, exit 0). Scan (d) also passes in both full integration runs. (2) Mutants that revert the fix are caught (both exit 1 by design): M1 (0130 removed) brings back exactly the audit's 24 served strings and fails 3 of the 4 scan tests (142 seeded violations; no reword audit events; the non-vacuity case cannot find 0130) (log 32); M2 (0130 without its kpi.freshness_scan row, a partial revert) leaves 2 served strings (that job's description in listJobSchedules and listJobOperations), and the scan fails on that one seeded value and on the changed audit counts (log 33). The clone was clean afterwards (logs 34, 34a). (3) My probe qa-rg-r5-seeded-0130.test.ts (log 31, 2/2 pass): P1 on a database migrated to 0129 and then changed as a user could have changed it, applying 0130 alone: rows a user touched (a service identity with updated_by set; a job description that is no longer the seeded text) are left byte for byte; kpi.freshness_scan, whose cron a user changed, is reworded with a version step from the user's version and the cron kept; every other column of the five tables equals its pre-0130 value; all earlier audit_event and service_identity_change rows are byte-identical; 0130 adds exactly the expected reword events (actor system, source migration); a second migrate applies nothing. P2: every parameterless GET of the contract as an administrator and as an auditor serves no string naming DG0-DG7. (4) Rendered screens (zz-qa-rg-r5-served-text-ui.spec.ts on with-stack.sh, log 36, 2/2 pass first time): Jobs, Job operations, all 49 service identities and all 16 automation rules, 68 screens per language, en and ar: 0 hits in visible text or form values. (5) Independent SQL scan of every text, array and JSON column of both stack databases (logs 35, 35b): no current value names DG0-DG7. The remaining matches are append-only history (the 'from' side of audit changes, the five audit_event.reason texts D-239 keeps, service_identity_change), the gate-submission snapshot disclaimer 'unrelated to the engineering delivery gates DG0-DG7' in demo data (a machine note inside the stored snapshot that no web screen renders; the allowlisted REPORTED_EXISTING_FINDINGS note), and, in demo data only, the current reason of the demo connector's service identity, 'The service identity of the synthetic demo connector demo-kpi-test-source (ADR-0053 §1).' (packages/db/src/demo/data/connectors.ts:91). That reason cites an ADR, not a DG gate, so the F-DG6-990 clause (no DG0-DG7 in served text) holds; I record it as an observation in my record, not as a defect. I agree with D-239 on the five audit reasons: they carry task and decision ids in the append-only trail (ADR-0004), and rewriting the trail would break a stronger invariant. One more observation: 0130 sets job_schedule.updated_by to NULL on the reworded kpi.freshness_scan row even where a user had changed its cron, so the row no longer names that user as its last updater; the user's change stays in the audit trail and the migration's own audit event names the system as the actor, so no history is lost.

My own Low, non-mandatory finding of this round, proposed for acceptance as an observation (it takes effect only if the release auditor adds the same acceptance). Rationale: the two out-of-order timestamps are in the histories of DG0 and DG5, which are APPROVED and closed. They change no gate decision, transition or validator result (--historical DG1-DG5 and --pipeline PASS), and they do not touch DG6 or the candidate. Correcting them is optional delivery-record hygiene. A validator rule that `at` never decreases would stop it recurring, and the orchestrator may still correct the two times with a note.
